title: onprem/airgap: offline bundle + vendoring updates for RKE2 (Ubuntu + Flatcar) + rollback tooling
author: Priya Kumar
release_notes:
- Add vendoring support for Ubuntu 22.04 and Flatcar in on-prem offline bundles.
- Include apt/yum/containers package tarballs and TUF metadata in offline artifacts.
- Add rollback tooling to safely revert air-gapped installs to previous offline bundle.
- Update Helm charts and installer to support checksum verification and distro-specific init hooks.
description:
Background: Customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped/on-prem environments have asked for broader distro support (Ubuntu LTS + Flatcar) and more robust vendoring of OS packages and container images so offline bundles can be consumed without internet access. This PR bundles vendored apt/yum artifacts and container images, updates the RKE2 distro hooks, and adds a small rollback utility to help operators revert to the previous bundle if an upgrade hits issues.

What this does: 1) Offline bundle generation: extend the bundle generator to collect Ubuntu 22.04 apt packages (deb), Flatcar packages, and snapshot container images; include signed TUF metadata and SHA256 manifests. 2) Vendoring: add script targets and Makefile entries (scripts/vendor-ubuntu.sh, scripts/vendor-flatcar.sh) to reproducibly fetch, cache, and sign artifacts for the bundle. 3) Installer changes: Helm chart values and templates updated to support distro detection, distro-specific preflight hooks, and verify-on-start checks that validate checksums and TUF signatures. 4) Rollback tooling: lightweight rollback script (bin/airgap-rollback) that restores previous bundle assets and rolls back Helm release to the pinned revision; integrates with our existing snapshot store. 5) Tests & CI: add integration test matrix job for offline bundle generation and smoke install on rke2-flatcar and rke2-ubuntu nodes (runs in infra with network access).

Notes: - The description contains the checklist and links inline. See Linear ENG-21234 for acceptance criteria and SUP-4021 for a customer reproduction. - TUF metadata rotation is supported via the new scripts; operator must rotate keys in KMS for production.

Checklist:
- [x] Bundle generator collects OS and container artifacts (scripts/vendor-*.sh)
- [x] Include TUF metadata and SHA256 manifest in offline tarballs
- [x] Helm chart updates to add distro hooks and image repository overrides
- [x] Add rollback script and documentation (docs/airgap-rollback.md)
- [x] Integration tests for rke2 Flatcar/Ubuntu smoke installs
- [x] Security review of vendored artifacts checksums and signing

Testing performed: Ran offline bundle generation end-to-end in CI with mocked mirror; validated install on rke2 single-node Flatcar VM and multi-node Ubuntu 22.04 cluster. Checked checksum/TUF verification path. Ran rollback flow and verified Helm release pointer restored to previous revision.

Risks and mitigations: The main risk is operators forgetting to rotate TUF keys; docs include explicit KMS rotation steps. Vendored OS packages increase bundle size (documented in release notes) and we advise selective package lists for constrained environments.

Related: pr-123456 (onprem-airgap-rke2-flatcar-support) and ENG-21234.
commits_summary: 1) feat: vendor scripts for ubuntu/flatcar and offline bundle generation; 2) chore: add Makefile targets and CI job; 3) helm: distro hooks and checksum verification; 4) feat: airgap rollback utility and docs; 5) test: add integration matrix for rke2 distros.
review_comments: Ethan Park: Please ensure the TUF root/private keys are never checked into the repo; add guidance for KMS-backed key storage. (resolved)
María González: Can we reduce default package list to keep bundle size in check? Suggest moving non-essential packages behind a flag. (addressed: packagelist split and Makefile flag added)
Noah Patel: CI integration failed originally due to flaky network mock; added retry logic in scripts/generate-offline-bundle.py and re-ran (CI green). (resolved)
Security team (automated scan): flagged potential unsigned container images in vendor list; scripts now verify image digests and include a verification step in generate-offline-bundle. (resolved)
Priya Kumar (author): replied with step-by-step upgrade/rollback instructions and added docs/airgap-rollback.md.
notes: This PR expands our supported distro footprint for on-prem/offline deployments and should be communicated to channel partners. Ops runbook updated in docs/airgap-rollback.md. Follow-up work: add selective package pruning UI in console (ENG-21789).
